 Order

Appellant/Insurance Company has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 assailing the award dated 31/10/2006 passed by Fourth Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track), Shivpuri in Claim Case No. 113/2006; whereby, respondents No. 1 and 2/claimant have been awarded a compensation of Rs. 3,11,900/- for the death of one Ramsevak, husband of respondent The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Mahila Brama on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56613235/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 No. 1 and father of respondent No. 2 and appellant and respondent No. 3 were fastened with the liability of payment of compensation amount.

2. Briefly stated facts of the case are that respondents no. 1 and 2 / Claimants filed a claim petition under Section 163 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal seeking a total compensation of Rs. 18,09,000/- for death of Ramsevak, husband of respondent No. 1 and father of respondent No. 2 pleading that on 18/4/2006 at about 4.00 am when deceased Ramsevak was going from Guna to Shivpuri by driving Matador No. MP08F0156, then opposite Indane Godown,
suddenly steering and brake system of the matador failed due to which vehicle turned turtle due to which deceased sustained grievous hurts and ultimately succumbed to the same on 25/4/2006 during treatment.
3.

The first contention raised by learned counsel for the appellant is that the deceased was possessing driving licence of driving Light Motor Vehicles and therefore, was not authorized to drive matador (goods vehicle) in absence of any endorsement in this regard over his licence, and therefore, Insurance Company cannot be held liable for payment of compensation amount.
Secondly, it is submitted that accident happened due to negligence of deceased himself.

4. On the other hand, respondents No. 1 and 2/claimants filed cross objections under Order XLI Rule 22 CPC vide I.A.No. 3989/2007 for enhancement of compensation amount as according to them deceased use to earn Rs. 4,000/- per month; whereas, the Tribunal has only assessed his income Rs. 2,100/- per month which is on the lower side.
No amount has been awarded under the head future prospect.
It is further submitted that amount awarded under the other heads is also on lower side.
In support of his contentions, he relied upon the decision of Apex Court in the matter of Raj Rani and Ors.
Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. and Ors., (2009)13SCC654, Rajendra Singh and Ors.

Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. and Ors., (2020)7SCC256 and decision of this Court in the matter of United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Rajkumari and Ors., (M.A.no. 476/2012 decided on 25/2/2019.)
5. None appeared on behalf of respondent No. 3.
6.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.
7. As regards contention of learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company that there was no endorsement over the driving licence of deceased to drive goods vehicle as in present case

,
Insurance Company cannot be fastened with the liability is concerned, in light of decision o Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Devangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. (2017) 14 SCC 663 has already been settled by holding that merely absence of endorsement to drive a commercial/goods vehicle will not deprive the victim or his legal heirs to claim compensation,
therefore, this issue is no more res integra, no further indulgence is required in this regard.
8.

entities.text: Mukund Devangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. (2017) 14 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As regards second contention of learned counsel for the appellant regarding negligence of deceased in driving the vehicle is concerned, since the claim case before the Claims Tribunal was filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, in such cases only involvement of the vehicle is The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Mahila Brama on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56613235/
2 liable to be tested on the anvil of evidence available and even if the accident happened due to negligence of driver then also the claimants are entitled to receive the compensation and claim case was maintainable.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Mahila Brama
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. As regards cross-objection filed on behalf of respondents No. 1 and 2/claimants, the incident in the present case is of the year 2006, and therefore, in the opinion of this Court, Claims Tribunal did not err in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs. 2100/- per month.

Further since the claim case was filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, the claimants were entitled to receive the compensation as per the structured formula basis as provided in second schedule only in which there is no provision for providing compensation under the head Future Prospect.
Therefore, in the opinion of this Court, the amount of compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper which needs no interference by this Court.
10. In light of aforesaid discussion, the decision cited by learned counsel for the respondents No. 1 and 2 move in different factual real and therefore, cannot be applied.
11. Cumulatively, in light of aforesaid discussion, the appeal fails and is hereby dismissed and the cross-objection filed vide I.A.No. 3989/2007 are also rejected.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
